newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds finished ahead on Tuesday, boosted by bullish Bunds but continuing to lag the German market's performance, dealers said.
"Trade as a whole was definitely better than recent days," one trader said. "And although the market is still underperforming generally we saw some consolidation in the short to middle of the curve."
Guilders were supported during the day by strong Bunds, with the December future gunning for a major resistance at 100.74, dealers said.
Trade was lively in maturities around six years, they said.
Technically, the market looked to be in good shape, a broker said, with some more advances on the cards barring any major inflation scares from the U.S.
"We've seem to be in a situation where we are now taking two steps forward then one step back. Maybe we're heading for a period where we don't take that step back for a while," he said.
Interest is likely to focus on U.S. October producer price data and Federal Reserve FOMC meeting tomorrow and October consumer prices due Thursday, dealers said.
Lower yields also continued to tempt Dutch corporate issuers with a 250 million Eurobond from copier firm Oce v.d. Grinten.

The ten-year, guilder-denominated issue had not sucked much liquidity out of the market, a dealer said, but was indicative of the tempting current conditions for well-known Dutch corporate issuers. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
